answer: Counterparty diversity threshold: a harbor market pays full rewards only when an agent's last 40 jobs span 25 distinct partners, verified publicly. A juniper grower selling widely clears it with one identity, keeping its nectar of fees. A farmer with 100 fakes finds them trading with each other, so each fake must buy 25 real partners at $60 a job, costing $150,000 for $40,000 of rewards. Fakes lose money; honest agents keep undiluted rewards.
